clue.text: Following each one, most importantly

parts.note: following means coming after
each one taken together is all of them

explanation.surface: A rule for a queue: behind every person, which matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to stress the decisive consideration, much like 'when all is said and done'.

clue.text: Help Jenny sit out

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, an ass

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of sit are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone tells Jenny to skip sitting this one out and lend a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to help someone is to aid or support them.

clue.text: Shown on the box, Leeds vet I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters of Leeds vet I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire vet suspects they have appeared on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broadcast on television has been shown on the small screen.

clue.text: A farce (mild farce) playing in a building in Oxford

indicators.note: playing about with the letters of the two farces rearranges them

explanation.surface: A theatre review: a gentle comedy staged inside a famous Oxford building.
explanation.walkthrough: The RADCLIFFE CAMERA is a round, domed reading room of Oxford's Bodleian Library.
explanation.definitionFit: The Radcliffe Camera is a landmark library building at the heart of Oxford University.

clue.text: Broad-minded artist included in defamatory statement

indicators.note: included in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a libel is a written defamatory statement
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A tolerant painter finds themself named in a libel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a liberal person is tolerant and open to other views.

clue.text: More work in chateau, topiary

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: There's more work to be done in a French castle's clipped gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is not the comparative but Sir Thomas More, who wrote Utopia (1516).
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's best-known book describes an imaginary ideal island state.

clue.text: Song from Cover Girl ("Send in the Clowns")

definitions.text: Song from Cover Girl ("Send in the Clowns")

parts.words: Song from Cover Girl ("Send in the Clowns")
parts.note: the band Queen (a queen is a cover girl on stamps and coins) recorded this song, and sending in the clowns is how a circus keeps performing whatever happens

explanation.surface: A reference to a number from the musical film Cover Girl, with a Sondheim ballad in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover Girl looks like the 1944 film, but it hints at Queen, the band; the bracketed Sondheim title echoes the showbiz motto of carrying on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1991 Queen single takes its title from the theatre motto that performances continue despite mishaps.

clue.text: Flat's electric current shown in diagram

indicators.note: shown in means one piece appears inside another

parts.note: a plan is a diagram
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: An apartment's wiring appears on the floor plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: flat country or a flat surface is plain, level and even.

clue.text: Views to look at, mostly in part of North Wales

parts.note: angles are points of view

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A tourist recommends scenic viewpoints in North Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Anglesey is the island county off the north-west tip of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglesey is an island off the north-west coast of Wales, a county in its own right.

clue.text: Fairy may produce horse and trap

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
a spider's web is a trap

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale image of a pony and a little carriage conjured up by magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' suggests a horse-drawn cart beside the horse, but here it is a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobweb is one of Titania's fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Weighty Roman coin American lost

indicators.note: lost means this piece goes missing from the coin

parts.note: the solidus was a gold coin of the later Roman Empire

explanation.surface: An American has mislaid a heavy ancient coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something solid is substantial and weighty.

clue.text: Embargo on developing a missile

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters of embargo on are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade embargo is imposed on a country developing a missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomerang is a curved throwing weapon, a missile hurled by hand.

clue.text: A very bad argument on singular Mayfair street

indicators.note: on in an across clue means coming after the piece it sits on

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
vile means very bad
a row is an argument

explanation.surface: A nasty quarrel breaks out about something singular in a smart London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Savile Row is the street of bespoke tailors in Mayfair, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Savile Row is a famous street in London's Mayfair district, known for gentlemen's tailoring.

clue.text: For this reason woman goes to church

parts.note: hen is informal for a woman
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Explaining why a woman attends church.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hence and therefore both introduce a consequence.

clue.text: Beneficial universal fuel, possibly containing sulphur

indicators.note: containing means holding another piece inside

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: possibly signals that fuel may be rearranged

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: An all-purpose fuel with sulphur in it might be beneficial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'universal fuel' reads as one phrase but splits: the U film rating, then 'possibly' shuffles fuel to EFUL, and 'containing' wraps that pair round the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something useful is helpful and beneficial.

clue.text: Rope below used to secure one, first of nine

indicators.note: to secure means to hold the other piece fast inside
used in the sense of worn or knocked about means the letters of below are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of nine is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to tie a rope below to make one safe, starting with number nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges BELOW to BOWLE; 'to secure' then places I and N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowline is a knot forming a fixed loop at the end of a rope, so it stands for the rope.

clue.text: Purposefully, I approach breeding ground

parts.note: to near is to approach
a nest is where birds breed

explanation.surface: Someone resolutely heads towards a bird's breeding site.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: doing something in earnest means doing it seriously and with determination.

clue.text: Dowdy behind counter outside

indicators.note: outside means this piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a fish is a gaming counter, a chip used in card games
the rump is the behind

explanation.surface: Someone unfashionably dressed stands at the back of a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a shop counter but is a FISH, an old card-game token.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frumpish describes someone dowdy and old-fashioned in dress.

clue.text: Set right about formal wear

parts.note: re means about or concerning
dress, as in evening dress, is formal wear

explanation.surface: Correcting someone's choice of evening clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to redress a wrong is to correct or remedy it.

clue.text: Excellent senior police officer, British

parts.note: super is short for superintendent, a senior police rank

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine British police chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: superb means of the very highest quality.

clue.text: Engineer's old letter displayed in British Legion

indicators.note: displayed in means shown inside the other piece

parts.note: BL is the abbreviation for the British Legion, the UK veterans' charity
a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet

explanation.surface: A letter from an engineer is put on show at a veterans' club.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel built Victorian Britain's Great Western Railway and steamships.
explanation.definitionFit: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was a celebrated nineteenth-century British civil engineer.

clue.text: Girl with male after white wine in Paris

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the other

parts.note: blanc is French for white, and un blanc is French for a glass of white wine
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A girl and a man sip white wine in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanche is a girl's name, as in Blanche DuBois.

clue.text: King Lear, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the name of eight English kings
the first name of the nonsense poet Lear, author of The Owl and the Pussy-cat

explanation.surface: A nod to Shakespeare's tragic king.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lear suggests Shakespeare, but the clue splits into a royal name and the poet Edward Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is a royal name and also the first name of the Victorian nonsense poet Lear.

clue.text: England's opener entering Marylebone Cricket Club, a place that attracts many visitors

indicators.note: entering means going inside another piece

parts.note: MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, which owns Lord's cricket ground in London

indicators.note: opener means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: England's opening batsman walks into the MCC pavilion at Lord's.
explanation.definitionFit: Mecca, Islam's holiest city, gives its name to any place drawing crowds of visitors.

clue.text: The sovereign hit on the head

definitions.meaning: the monarchy or the reigning monarch
informal for striking someone on the top of the skull

explanation.definitionFit: The monarchy is called the Crown, and to crown someone is slang for hitting them on the head.

clue.text: Intoxicated, pedlar set off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or disordered, so the letters of pedlar set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunken hawker sets off on his rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: plastered means very drunk.

clue.text: One short joke about certain people equal in measurement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
some means certain people, as in 'some say'

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a trick is a practical joke

explanation.surface: Someone tells a brief gag about a particular group, which may be fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometric means having equal dimensions or measurements.

clue.text: Oxygen given to huge Greek character

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
mega is slang for huge

explanation.surface: A giant Greek figure is given some air.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Girl like Ada and another one in hot hospital

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: H is short for hot, as on a tap
Anna is another girl's name that, like Ada, reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: Two girls end up in a stuffy hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like Ada' means a palindromic name, which describes both the answer and ANNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannah is a girl's name that reads the same backwards, just as Ada does.

clue.text: One feeding ungulates brought back together again

indicators.note: feeding means going into the middle of the other piece
brought back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: deer are hoofed mammals, ungulates
a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: A keeper feeding hoofed animals that have been brought home.
explanation.walkthrough: DEER serves as a plural, so it matches 'ungulates'; 'brought back' gives REED and 'feeding' slips the one in, while 'together again' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reunited describes people joined together again after a separation.
